summary: WorldEntity audit found two additional runtime-boundary gaps on current main/PR #271: required capture APIs silently accept nil as empty durable state because cloneState also implements constructor defaulting, and createRegistry silently treats false capacity as omitted while non-number hostile tables can reach numeric comparison metamethods before rejection.
evidence: PR #271 issue comment 5249983545 records both findings and requested regression coverage.
WorldEntity.captureState(record, nil :: any) reaches cloneState(nil), becomes {}, and advances stateRevision; captureRegistered inherits the same behavior despite a non-optional PlainData contract.
WorldEntity.createRegistry(false :: any) evaluates false through `duplicateDiagnosticCapacity or DEFAULT`, silently selecting the default capacity instead of rejecting malformed input.

createRegistry passes runtime input directly to assertFiniteNumber, whose comparisons occur without an initial type check; a table can therefore reach comparison metamethods such as __lt before fail-closed rejection.
The hostile diagnostic-formatting fix should also audit fidelityRank and unknown registered-ID formatting, which interpolate runtime values at public typed boundaries.
